history.summary: Devi (Shakti) temple in Nellore city founded in 1968 by Sri Sri Arul Jyoti Natarajamurthy Swami with the blessings of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham; the idol of Sri Rajarajeshwari was consecrated and Maha Kumbhabhishekam performed on 06.03.1975 by Kanchi Peethadhis Sri Jayendra Saraswati and Pushpagiri Peethadhis Sri Vidyananda Nrisimha Bharati. Built under the patronage of Swargiya Ratnaswami Modiliar through his funds and devotee donations, on land granted by the then Nellore District Collector. Sub-temples in the complex: Sri Gayatri Ammavari Devasthanam, Sri Sundareswara Swami Vari Devasthanam and Navagraha Mandapams.

name: Sri Rajarajeshwari Temple
town_description: Nellore, headquarters of Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district, is a major coastal city on the south bank of the Penna river in southern Andhra Pradesh. Known for its vast paddy fields, the historic Ranganathaswamy Temple, the Nellore Cheruvu tank and nearby Pulicat Lake, it is a trade and education hub of the region.

travel.airport: Tirupati Airport (TIR), Renigunta is the nearest public airport; Chennai is the nearest international airport
travel.railway: Nellore Railway Station - well connected to New Delhi, Vijayawada, Chennai, Hyderabad, Howrah, Bengaluru and Kanyakumari
travel.road: Well connected by road and bus to Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam and Chennai

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Fridays and Navaratri draw the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (per the district government temple page)
